questions.prompt: According to Screaming Architecture, what should a system's top-level structure 'scream'?

options.text: What the system is for — its use cases and domain

questions.explanation: The loudest thing about the structure should be the system's purpose (e.g., 'health-care system'), not the framework, which is a delivery detail.

questions.prompt: Does Screaming Architecture mean you should avoid frameworks?

options.text: No — it means don't let the framework be the organizing principle; keep it an outer, replaceable detail
Yes — hand-roll everything the framework does
No — because frameworks belong in the entities layer

questions.explanation: It's about organizing around intent and keeping the framework at the edge — not about discarding frameworks.

questions.prompt: Organizing top-level folders by domain capability (billing/, accounts/) rather than technical role is called package-by-______.
questions.explanation: Package-by-feature groups a capability's parts together and screams the domain; package-by-layer scatters features and screams the framework.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to refactor a top-level structure from package-by-layer to an intent-revealing package-by-feature.

items.text: Gather its use cases, entity, gateway, and adapter into one folder
Expose a single public entry point for the feature
Add a lint rule enforcing the feature's boundary

questions.explanation: Group each capability's parts together behind one entry point and enforce the boundary, so the structure screams the domain rather than the framework.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: The framework/UI used to deliver the app — a detail
Grouping by technical role; screams the framework
Grouping by capability; screams the domain
A layout that documents what the system does

questions.explanation: Screaming Architecture favors intent-revealing, feature-based structure with the delivery mechanism kept as an outer detail.

questions.prompt: Which are benefits of an intent-revealing, package-by-feature structure? Select all that apply.

options.text: Developers can find and change a capability quickly
A feature's parts stay cohesive and close together
The framework decision stays visible at the edge and replaceable
It forces you to hand-code routing and serialization

questions.explanation: Feature-based structure aids navigation, cohesion, and keeping the framework a replaceable detail. It does not require replacing what frameworks provide.
